translation.text: And I lifted up my hands in righteousness[a], and I blessed the Holy and Great One; and I spoke with the spirit of my mouth and with the tongue of flesh, which God has made for the children of the flesh of men, so that they might speak with it; and he gave them spirit and tongue and mouth[b], so that they might speak by them.

footnotes.text: Or 'I spoke by the spirit of my mouth.' The Ge'ez term can denote breath, spirit, or wind; here 'breath' best fits the list of speech faculties.
The wording is deliberately bodily: literally, 'the children of the flesh of men.' The phrase underscores human creatureliness rather than using a smoother generic term.

source.text: ቡሩክ፡ አንተ፡ እግዚኦ፡ ንጉሥ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ወኃያል፡ በዕበየ፡ ዚአከ፡ እግዚኦ፡ ኵሉ፡ ፍጥረት፡ ሰማይ፡ ንጉሠ፡ ነገሥት፡ ወአምላከ፡ ኵሉ፡ ዓለም፡ ወ*መላኵትከ፡ ወመንግሥትከ፡ ወዕበይከ፡ ይነብር፡ *ለዓለም፡ ወለዓለመ፡ ዓለም፡ ወለኵሉ፡ ትውልደ፡ ትውልድ፡ ስልጣንከ፡ ወኵሎሙ፡ ሰማያት፡ መንበርከ፡ ለዓለም፡ ወ*ኵላ፡ ምድር፡ መካይደ፡ እገሪከ፡ *ለዓለም፡ ወ*ለ*ዓለመ፡ ዓለመ።

translation.text: Blessed are you[a], O Lord, great King and mighty in your greatness, Lord of all the creation of heaven, King of kings and God of all the world. And your kingship and your kingdom and your greatness endure forever and ever, and your authority is for all generations of generations. And all the heavens are your throne forever[d][c][b], and the whole earth is the footstool of your feet forever and ever.

footnotes.text: The term rendered 'your majesty' is textually difficult in the OCR witness; it may also be understood as 'your dominion' or 'your glory.'
The phrase 'all creation of heaven' is literal to the Ge'ez sequence and may mean 'all heavenly creation.'
Compare the biblical throne-and-footstool image in Isa 66:1; the Enochic verse uses the same kind of cosmic royal imagery without requiring identical wording.
Or 'and through all generations of generations. All the heavens'.

source.text: እስመ፡ አንተ፡ ገበርከ፡ ወ*ለኵሉ፡ አንተ፡ ትመልክ፡ ወ*ኢይጸንዐከ፡ ግብር፡ *ወኢ፡ ፩[ወአሐቲ፡] ጥበብ፡ ኢትሐልፍ፡ *እምንባራተ፡ ምንባሪከ፡ ወኢትትመየጥ፡ ኢእምገጽከ፡ ወአንተ፡ ኵሎ፡ *ታአምር፡ ወትሬኢ፡ ወትሰምዕ፡ ወአልቦ፡ ዘይትኀባእ፡ እምኔከ፡ [እስመ፡ ኵሎ፡ ትሬኢ።]

translation.text: For you have made all things[a], and over all things you rule; and no deed is too hard for you, and not even a single wisdom passes beyond the throne of your dwelling, nor turns away from before your face. And you know all things, and see, and hear, and there is nothing hidden from you[d][c][b], for you see all things.

footnotes.text: The clause 'not even a single wisdom passes beyond the throne of your dwelling' is difficult in the Ge'ez. It may refer to no wise plan, thought, or matter being beyond God's royal dwelling-place.
The final sentence repeats the theme of total divine knowledge; some witnesses appear to preserve an explicit concluding line, 'for you see all things.'
Or 'For you have made all things, and over all things you rule'.

translation.text: And now the angels of your heavens have transgressed[c][b][a], and your wrath is upon the flesh of men until the great day of judgment.

footnotes.text: The closing words are difficult in the Ethiopic OCR. The sense is likely a qualifier such as 'of judgment' or 'of recompense' attached to 'the great day.'
'The flesh of man' preserves the source imagery; the phrase likely refers collectively to humankind in its mortal condition.
Or 'let the angels of your heavens make petition, and let your wrath be upon the flesh of man until the great day that belongs to judgment.'.

translation.text: And now, O God and Lord and great King, I plead and ask that You establish my prayer for me: preserve for me a remnant on the earth, and do not destroy all human flesh or leave the earth bare, so that destruction would endure forever.[a]

footnotes.text: The term provisionally rendered remnant may be understood as posterity or descendants. The closing negative request concerns the continuation of humanity and the earth in this ancient prayer; the complete selected source runs across the page boundary.

source.text: ወይእዜኒ፡ እግዚእየ፡ አጥፍእ፡ *እምዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ሥጋ፡ እንተ፡ አምዐዐተከ፡ ወሥጋ፡ *ጽድቅ፡ ወርትዕ፡ አቅም፡ ለተክለ፡ ዘርእ፡ ለዓለም፡ ወኢትሰውር፡ ገጸከ፡ እምስእለተ፡ ገብርከ፡ እግዚኦ።

translation.text: And now, my Lord, remove from the earth the flesh that provoked Your wrath, but establish the flesh of righteousness and uprightness as a plant of enduring seed; and do not hide Your face from the prayer of Your servant, O Lord.[a]

footnotes.text: The plant/seed expression is the prayer’s image for preserving a righteous line. This is the speaker’s ancient petition, not an instruction to readers or a claim about any modern population. The exact duration and seed phrasing require independent scan review.
